_licensingNote: Original, not an SCP. Regional Site 19, its five rooms, its operations board and its dossiers were authored for this build. The eight designations in this file are provisional markers this project assigned to its own anomalies and are not SCP numbers: GDD §25.3 assigns a final designation only after an attribution record exists, and no attribution record exists because there is nothing third-party here to attribute. licensingRecordId is null because there is no third-party material to record, and this note is what makes that null mean 'checked, and here is why' rather than 'nobody has looked at this one'. See content/provenance.json.
_note: The Foundation home base as DATA — GDD §13, cut to the compact five-room slice of §26.2: operations room, armory/logistics counter, archive terminal, small research station, containment observation corridor. §13.1 asks that preparing for a mission take minutes and not a commute, so this is a screen with tabs rather than a walkable building, and every room is one page. The eight core areas of §13.2 are folded into five: the research station carries the isolation bench that a full site would give the Medical Wing, and the logistics counter carries the Engineering Bay's repair queue. That is not a shortcut, it is the fiction — an underfunded regional facility has one room doing three jobs, and §13.3 says the site begins underfunded.
_effectsNote: Every `effect` key is validated against DEFAULT_EFFECTS in src/sim/progression.js and the file REFUSES to load if it names one no system reads. An upgrade that quietly did nothing would fail §13.3's 'upgrades visibly add capability' without ever failing a test.
standing: Regional Site 19 runs on a regional grant, one vehicle, and whatever the last operation brought back. Nothing here is new and two of the rooms were something else first.

regionalStatus.weather: Overcast, 4C, wind from the north-east. No change expected before the window closes.
regionalStatus.region: Three counties, one duty squad, and a coroner who has stopped asking questions.
regionalStatus.readiness: One vehicle. One command point. Everything you take is everything you have.

_noticesNote:
GDD §25.4 requires attribution to be reachable from the main menu rather than buried in end credits, and §23 Milestone 6 gates on store, credits, EULA, privacy and support materials being approved. `notices` is those documents AS CONTENT, so the screen that renders them contains no prose of its own and a change of wording is a content edit rather than a code edit.

SHAPE, for whatever renders it: `notices.documents` is an ORDERED array. Each document is { id, title, summary, sections[] }; each section is { heading, body[], bullets[] } where `body` is an array of paragraphs and `bullets` is optional. Every string is PLAIN TEXT with no markup — escape it on the way out. Nothing here is a translation key: unlike the room furniture, these are legal and privacy statements whose exact wording is the point, and a locale that paraphrased one would be making a different claim. `notices.room` names the room the documents hang off.

EVERY FACTUAL CLAIM IN THE PRIVACY DOCUMENT WAS READ OUT OF THE CODE, not out of the comments — which matters, because two of the comments are wrong. See docs/day-one-operations.md and docs/licensing-audit.md findings 8 and 9.

documents.title: Credits
documents.summary: Who made this, what it was built on, and what was imported rather than re-invented.

sections.heading: The build
body: Containment Detail, the browser build. One page, no installer, no account. Everything it needs is committed alongside it.
It is a second implementation of one design bible, and the bible came first. Where this build and the document disagree, the document is the authority and the disagreement is a bug in one of them.

sections.heading: Imported, not re-invented
body: The design bible, the first anomaly, the first map and the equipment manifest come from Dumb-Tony/ContainmentDetail — the same game in Unity, by the same author. They were carried across rather than written again.

The draught is that repository's own content file, extended here with the fields this simulation reads. The cold-storage floor came over at content revision 0.1.0 and the equipment manifest at 0.2.0; each file records what was added on the way in. Everything since — the other seven anomalies, the other three maps, the site, the onboarding — was authored here.

sections.heading: Third-party code
body: Two libraries are vendored into this build. Both are MIT, both are unmodified, and both carry their licence text in the directory beside the code, because MIT requires the notice to travel with the software rather than to be recorded somewhere near it.
bullets: Three.js r128 — MIT. Copyright 2010-2021 Three.js Authors, transcribed from the library's own header. Full text in assets/lib/r128/LICENSE.

PeerJS 1.5.4 — MIT, on the library's own declaration in its embedded package metadata. The vendored bundle carries no copyright notice at all and this project has not invented one; the gap is recorded rather than filled in. Full text and the record in assets/lib/peerjs-1.5.4/LICENSE.
The digest of each is pinned and re-checked on every audit run, which is what makes unmodified a fact rather than a claim.

sections.heading: What is not third-party
body: Everything else. All the simulation, interface, tooling and content in this build is original to the project.

There is no bitmap art anywhere in it, no third-party texture, and no typeface file. The interface is your system fonts and the world is generated geometry — which is also why there is nothing else to credit here.

documents.title: Attribution and licensing
documents.summary: Where the material came from. The short version: none of it is SCP material.

sections.heading: No SCP material is in this build
body: Every anomaly here is original. Not adapted, not paraphrased, not derived — written for this game.

That is not a promise, it is a measurement, and it is re-taken every time the audit runs. Every content file states where its material came from. Every licensing record is null AND says in a sentence why it is null, which is the difference between checked and forgotten. No file names an SCP designation.

sections.heading: Why every designation says provisional
body: The eight designations you see on case files are markers this project assigned to its own anomalies. They are marked provisional because a final designation is assigned only once an attribution record exists, and no attribution record exists — because there is nothing here that belongs to anybody else to attribute.
A designation that quietly lost its provisional marker would be the moment this project started making a licensing claim nobody had cleared. The audit fails on it.

sections.heading: If that ever changes
body: The attribution record has twelve required fields — the article and its title, its URL, its authors, the wiki branch, the revision or access date, what was adapted, what was changed, the required licence and notice, the associated assets and their own sources, the internal owner, the legal review status, and where the credit appears.

The table exists in this build with no rows in it. That is deliberate: an empty table with a schema fails loudly the first time somebody adds derived content without a record, and an absent table is what lets that content ship with no record at all.

sections.heading: Checked rather than asserted
body: None of the above is held in anybody's head. A script re-derives all of it from the repository on every run: the digest of every vendored file, the licence text beside it, every provenance declaration, every designation, and every file in the tree that is neither original nor declared.
It needs no build step, no network and no browser, because an audit that only the person who wrote it can run is not an audit.

documents.title: Privacy
documents.summary: What is stored, where it is stored, and what leaves your machine.

sections.heading: Nothing is collected
body: There is no analytics, no telemetry, no crash reporting, no account, no advertising and no cookie. Nothing is sent anywhere about how you play, how long you played, or whether you finished.

The crash banner is the usual place a game grows a quiet exception, so it is worth being exact: it makes no network request of any kind. When something goes wrong it puts the report on the screen and copies it to your clipboard if you press the button. That is the whole delivery mechanism, and you are the one who delivers it.

sections.heading: What is stored, and it is stored on your machine
body: The game keeps six things in your browser's local storage, under this site's own address. They never leave it unless you carry them somewhere yourself.
bullets: Your campaign — operations completed, custodies verified, requisition and research, clearance, department standing, what you have learned about each anomaly, upgrades and fitted equipment, your squad roster, what is in containment, and your debrief history.
A quarantine copy — if the game ever finds a save it cannot read, it copies that save aside verbatim before starting fresh, so a bad load cannot destroy a campaign silently.
Your settings — controls, captions, colour and contrast, camera, volumes, assists and safety options. Numbers, switches and key codes; no text you typed.
Your callsign — the name you type before deploying, at most fourteen characters.
Rooms you have joined — up to eight, each with its room code, the room name that was typed, the operation label and when it was. No callsigns.
A language preference, which this build reads and never writes.

sections.heading: One thing to know if you play with other people
body: When an operation ends, the machine running the simulation writes the squad into its campaign roster so injuries and history follow the right operative. That roster holds names — and after a co-op operation, the names of the people you played with are among them.

Concretely: up to five roster entries, each at most fourteen characters, holding the callsigns other players typed, kept in the host's browser storage until that storage is cleared. Nobody else receives them and they are not sent anywhere. But they are on disk, and this page would be wrong not to say so.

sections.heading: What leaves your machine
body: A solo operation makes no external request at all. The page loads its own files and nothing else happens.
Hosting or joining is different, because two browsers cannot find each other unaided:
bullets: A signalling broker at 0.peerjs.com introduces the two browsers. It sees the room identifier — which, for a named room, contains the room name you typed — and the connection details the browsers exchange, and those include IP addresses. It carries no game traffic: once the link is up, everything goes browser to browser.

Connection setup also uses the networking library's default helpers: a public address-discovery server at stun.l.google.com, and, if the two browsers cannot reach each other directly, a relay at eu-0.turn.peerjs.com or us-0.turn.peerjs.com. Traffic that goes through the relay is still end-to-end between browsers, but it does pass through a machine that is not yours.

Between players: your callsign, where you are and where you are looking, what you do, and the shared state of the operation. The last few squad-feed lines travel as written sentences, and a sentence can contain somebody's callsign.
If you advertise a room, a stranger's browser can see the code, the room name, the operation and how many seats are taken — never who is in them.

sections.heading: The record the game keeps of a mission holds no free text
body: The event log a mission produces is a fixed vocabulary of things that happened: a state change and its cause, an operative down, evidence logged, a procedure committed. It is capped and it is in memory.

The one part of the game that carries written prose — the squad feed, which says things like somebody is down, get to them — is dispatched to the screen and the audio cue and deliberately kept out of that record, because prose is the one thing that can contain a name somebody typed.

sections.heading: Clearing it
body: Deleting your campaign and resetting your settings are both available in the game.

Being straight about the rest: the game has no button that clears your saved callsign, your list of recent rooms, or the quarantine copy of an unreadable save. Clearing site data for this address in your browser removes all six at once, and that is the only complete way to do it in this build.

sections.heading: How this page is kept true
body: Every claim above was read out of the running code rather than out of a comment near it, and the ones that are checked automatically are checked on every test run: that the crash boundary makes no request, that nothing outside the networking module sends anything anywhere, that a room listing carries a seat count and not a seat holder, that the recent-rooms list holds no callsign, and that a name never reaches the durable event log.

Two of the claims are not checked automatically, and are named as gaps in the project's own audit rather than left to be discovered: the campaign roster described above, and the connection helpers the networking library reaches by default.

documents.title: Terms of use
documents.summary: Plain words, honestly labelled. This is not legal advice and no lawyer has read it.

sections.heading: What this is
body: A game you can play in a browser at no charge. There is nothing to buy, nothing to subscribe to, no account to make, and no payment is taken anywhere in it.
It is a prototype in active development. Things will break, saves may need migrating, and a build may be rolled back to an earlier one at short notice.

sections.heading: No warranty, and that is not boilerplate
body: The game is provided as is, without warranty of any kind. It is not fit for any particular purpose and nobody is liable for anything that follows from using it.

The practical version: your campaign lives in your browser's storage. Clearing site data deletes it, a browser in private mode will not keep it, and there is no copy anywhere else because nothing is sent anywhere. If it matters to you, it is worth knowing that before it happens rather than afterwards.

sections.heading: Third-party components
body: This build includes Three.js and PeerJS, both under the MIT licence. Their notices travel with the build, in the directory beside each library, and your use of those components is under their licences and not under these terms.

sections.heading: The project's own code
body: The source is public and no open-source licence has been chosen for it, which is a factual statement about the repository rather than an invitation. If you want to reuse part of it, ask.
This paragraph, and this page, are a description of where things stand. They are not legal advice.

sections.heading: Not affiliated with anything
body: This game is not endorsed by, affiliated with, or connected to the SCP Wiki or its contributors. It contains no SCP-derived material — see the attribution page, which explains how that is checked rather than merely stated.

No qualified intellectual-property attorney has reviewed this project. That status is recorded in the repository as not obtained, deliberately, because recording it honestly is the only version of that clause worth having.

documents.title: Support
documents.summary: What to do when it breaks, and what the reference number in the banner is for.

sections.heading: The banner with a reference on it
body: When the game throws, a banner appears carrying a reference that looks like CD-1A2B3C4 and, on its first line, the build the game is running.

The reference is derived from where the fault happened rather than from what it said, so the same bug produces the same reference on any machine — which is what makes two reports comparable. It moves when the code moves, though, so it identifies a bug in a build rather than a bug on its own. Always quote the build line with it.

sections.heading: Press Copy report
body: The button next to the banner puts the whole report on your clipboard. It contains the build, which operation and scenario and seed you were on, the page address without its host, how many faults there were and how many were distinct, a reference and a message and a stack for each, and any file that failed to load.

There is no personal data in it by design, with one honest exception: an error message can quote text you typed, most likely a callsign. The report is on your screen before it is anywhere else, so read it before you paste it.

sections.heading: Where to send it
body: Open an issue on the project's repository, Dumb-Tony/ContainmentDetailWeb, and paste the report in. The reference in the title and the build line in the body are enough to find it.
Nothing sends itself. If you do not send it, nobody sees it.

sections.heading: Why it sometimes stops instead of carrying on
body: After the same fault three times, or thirty faults in all, the game stops rather than continuing.

That is a decision and not a failure to recover. A game that throws once a frame and keeps painting looks like it is working: the world animates, and every number on your display quietly stopped updating twenty seconds ago. You would read a custody timer that had frozen and act on it. A game that cannot keep its promises should say so and stop.

sections.heading: If your campaign comes back empty
body: Almost always this means the build you are on is older than the one that wrote your save — after a rollback, for instance. When that happens the game refuses the save rather than reading it wrongly, copies it aside untouched, and starts you fresh for the session. Your campaign is not gone; this build simply will not read it.

Opening the newer build again picks it up where you left off. ⚠ Being straight about a rough edge: this build does not yet put that sentence on the screen when it happens, so an empty campaign after a rollback currently arrives with no explanation. It is a known gap and it is written down.

sections.heading: Before you report anything else
body: Two things account for most of it. Serve the game over http rather than opening the file directly, or the module loads fail. And if a co-op session will not connect, it is almost always the connection helpers rather than the game — see the privacy page for exactly which hosts a session contacts.

rooms.name: Operations room
rooms.purpose: Where an incident becomes an operation. The board, the map table, the regional picture, and the readiness check that says whether the squad can actually go.
rooms.furniture: A map table with a cracked overlay, a wall board, and a radio set that predates the site.
allows: Read the mission board and take the authorised operation
Read the regional and weather picture before committing
Check squad readiness, including who is carrying an injury

upgrades.name: Backup power
upgrades.blurb: A generator and a proper charging bench. Cells go out full instead of go out.
upgrades.visible: The corridor lights stop dropping when the compressor cycles, and every issued item leaves with an extra minute on it.

upgrades.name: Additional vehicle bay
upgrades.blurb: A second vehicle means the manifest stops being a single wager.
upgrades.visible: Two more volume on every cargo manifest, for good.

rooms.name: Armory and logistics counter
rooms.purpose: Loadouts, maintenance, the cargo manifest, and equipment recovery. The counter is also the repair queue, because there is no engineering bay and the same person does both.
rooms.furniture: A roller shutter, a parts bin, and a whiteboard listing what did not come back.
allows: Fit an equipment sidegrade, or refit the standard tool
Requisition new variants against department standing
Read what the last operation failed to recover

upgrades.name: Specialised storage
upgrades.blurb: Climate-controlled racking with sensor ports, and a bonded cage for recovered gear.
upgrades.visible: Two more holding positions in the corridor, and written-off equipment costs a quarter less to reorder.

rooms.name: Archive terminal
rooms.purpose: Case files, mission history, the anomaly codex, and the attribution record. One terminal, one chair, and everything the site has ever filed.
rooms.furniture: A terminal on a desk that was a canteen table.
allows: Read the debrief history, dimension by dimension
Read the case file on anything the site has encountered
Read the attribution and licensing record

upgrades.name: Expanded archives
upgrades.blurb: Proper indexing and a second terminal, so a case file can be cross-read against the last twenty operations.
upgrades.visible: Twenty operations on file instead of twelve, and a tenth more analytical yield from everything you bring back.

upgrades.name: Training and simulation space
upgrades.blurb: A room with a floor plan taped out on it and a procedure rehearsal each week. Departments notice a squad that practises.
upgrades.visible: Every standing gain is worth about a sixth more.

rooms.name: Research station
rooms.purpose: Sample analysis, research projects, and the isolation bench the site uses to treat exposure because there is no medical wing.
rooms.furniture: A fume hood, a sample fridge, and one isolation bed behind a curtain.
allows: Spend research data on prototypes and analytical unlocks
Read what the site knows about an anomaly, and what it would take to know more
Treat an injured operative, or decide not to and field them anyway

upgrades.name: Better medical isolation
upgrades.blurb: A second bed, a real airlock, and a supply cupboard that is not shared with the sample fridge.
upgrades.visible: Two operatives can be treated in the same rotation, and a course costs less than half again.

rooms.name: Containment observation corridor
rooms.purpose: A short run of cells and monitor feeds. Whatever the site is holding is held here, and the corridor's job is to record what holding it costs.
rooms.furniture: Three cells, a monitor bank with one dead channel, and a clipboard nobody has replaced with a tablet.
allows: Read the operational history of everything in custody
Read the maintenance record and what the next check is due
See which holding positions are free before committing to an operation

upgrades.name: Stronger perimeter monitoring
upgrades.blurb: Sensors on the corridor and the fence line, reporting continuously instead of when somebody walks past.
upgrades.visible: Checks fall due two operations further apart, and the regional grant goes up because the auditors can see the logs.

operations.name: Cold storage, level 2
operations.distance: Forty minutes out. Sub-level, no surface exposure.
operations.mandate: Establish custody of the anomaly on level 2 and transfer it to the stair head.
conditions: Mains down six days. Two circuits, both dead.
One surviving crew member waiting at the stair head.
Plant log reports the chiller ran eleven days against a four-hour duty cycle.

operations.name: Cold storage, aisle B
operations.distance: The same floor as the last one. You already know the way.
operations.mandate: Establish custody of the figure reported in aisle B and transfer it to the stair head.
optional: Preserve a dust sample from the ring
conditions: Repeat sighting, four calls in one shift, nothing found on four walks.
The supervisor watched it on camera instead and it stayed put for six hours.
Fourteen unexplained brownouts on the storage circuit, none over nine seconds.
operations._note: The SAME MAP as op-cold-storage-2 and a completely different operation — GDD 15.2's epistemic and operational variation. The board is the one place a player sees that the building is a constant and the incident is the variable.

operations.name: Ashlar House, ninth floor
operations.distance: Two hours out, then nine floors on foot. The lift is out and the stair is the only way anything leaves.
operations.mandate: Establish custody of the anomaly on the ninth floor and transfer it to the east landing.
optional: Recover the contractor day book intact
conditions: Condemned crosswall block, decanted eleven months, stripped back to the frame.
Both circuits are on the contractor temporaries. Nothing is locked; everything is stuck open.
The drained district-heating gallery runs the full width of the floor behind the store rooms.
operations._note: THE SAME ANOMALY as op-cold-storage-2, on different geometry — the mirror of what the aisle B operation does. GDD 15.2 varies the incident against a constant building; this varies the building against a constant incident, and a squad that arrives with the cold store playbook has brought the right tools in the wrong quantity to the wrong end of a very long walk.

operations.name: Cold storage, the stocktake
operations.distance: The same forty minutes, the same stair, the third time.
operations.mandate: Recover the discrepancy in full, verify the count against the stocktake, and transfer it to the stair head.
optional: Log nothing into the case that does not belong there
Read the second clerk's sheet before committing to a count
conditions: Two independent stocktakes returned the same wrong number.
Nothing on this floor has been reported as moving, and nobody has been hurt.
The clerk who ran the second count is at the stair head and has her sheet.
operations._note: THE THIRD FAMILY (GDD 26.2: distributed-object recovery and verification) and the third operation on this one floor. Nothing hunts you here, there is no fence, and the failure state is arithmetic. A squad that has done the other two walks in knowing where the breakers are and which aisle is long, and none of that is the answer — familiarity is the trap.

operations.name: Blackthorn Reserve, north plantation
operations.distance: Ninety minutes, then a forest track. Two ways across the drainage channel and one of them is gated.
operations.mandate: Establish custody of whatever is in the north plantation and transfer it to the vehicles.
optional: Take the contractor's statement before deploying
conditions: Mains down across the reserve. One generator, not running since the withdrawal.
A tree-safety crew withdrew; one of them walked out on his hands and knees.
The duty ranger spent a further night in the station with everything switched off and reported nothing at all.
operations._note: THE SLICE'S FOREST MAP AND ITS AUDITORY FAMILY, which belong together. Blackthorn has no lanes — 41.5% of it has all twenty-four escape rays open and none of it is fenced bare — so it cannot host a fence incident honestly, and the caller does not want one. It is restrained by SILENCE, which is available everywhere and weighs nothing. A squad that arrives with the draught playbook deploys four humming objects and builds itself a beacon.

operations.name: Blackthorn reserve, the generator
operations.distance: The reserve again. The gate code has not changed.
operations.mandate: Establish custody of whatever is riding the compound generator and transfer it to the vehicles.
conditions: The set has run eleven years without a break; the one week it was pulled, the frost ring moved to the spare.
Fuel consumption up four per cent a month for a year. Two meters, same creep.
Reserve staff check the generator by ear from the hut door. None of them can say when that started.
operations._note: The second operation on the reserve, and the counter-lesson to the first: the July order pinned in the hut says no powered sound sources on this floor, and the thing in the generator is dislodged by attention and rehoused by warmth. The squad that learned silence here must now run something warm and loud on purpose, at night, with the compound lights sagging. 15.2 both ways: the compound transfers, the playbook does not.

operations.name: Coldharbour cold storage, level 2
operations.distance: Forty minutes. The same goods lift, the same stair, the same floor you have been on three times.
operations.mandate: Establish custody of whatever is at the north end of the west run and transfer it to the stair head.
conditions: One fatality on the floor since Tuesday. He was warm when they found him on the Wednesday.
One powered object on this level in eleven weeks, and it failed at 06:14 on Tuesday morning.
The fixed camera at the head of the west run has been turned to the wall and taped over from the aisle side. Nobody has claimed it.
operations._note: THE FOURTH OPERATION ON THIS FLOOR, and the one that punishes knowing it. A squad arrives with three operations' worth of correct knowledge about cold storage level 2 and every piece of it is aimed at the wrong thing: nothing here is fenced by anything ever, a camera anywhere near the case makes the operation stutter, and restoring the mains only makes the floor bright enough to look at things by — which is the failure mode. The one habit that survives is the one nobody thinks of as a habit: get the case powered before anything else happens.

operations.name: Ashlar House, Flat 5
operations.distance: The same two hours and the same nine floors. You already know which stair.
operations.mandate: Establish custody of whatever is in Flat 5 and transfer it to the east landing.
optional: Recover the fitter's helmet camera intact
conditions: Five flats stripped out, the sixth abandoned after three half days.
One man off with a cold burn and a fractured wrist; the other walked out and will not go back.
The watchman has walked the ninth in the dark for four months and reports no trouble.
operations._note: THE SECOND OPERATION ON THE NINTH FLOOR, and the one that inverts what the first taught. The gallery draught is a journey and a fence; this never leaves one flat and there is nothing to build. Ashlar's thirty-eight plasterboard walls were useless against the draught and are the answer here: they stop a sightline and nothing else, so a wall on this floor is privacy rather than protection. A squad that has done aisle B will deploy a camera on it out of habit and hold it rigid for that camera's whole battery.

operations.name: Harrowbank switching compound
operations.distance: An hour and fifty on the trunk road, then four miles of unmade track. The compound gate is padlocked and the incomer is open, so nothing on the site has power until somebody walks in and throws it.
operations.mandate: Establish custody of whatever is on the north half of the compound, together with every part of it that is loose on the ground, and transfer the case to the vehicle.
optional: Lift a sample of the ground dust before the case is closed
conditions: Three-man gang withdrawn after two days. One of them is in hospital with a crush injury and nothing fell on him.
Stone barrowed out to the skip was back in the yard by the afternoon. Twice, on two weighbridge tickets twenty-six hours apart.
The compound has been dark for nine days. Both yard circuits are dead and the two breakers are in different halves of the site.
operations._note: THE FIRST OPERATION ON A COMPOUND RATHER THAN IN A BUILDING, and the first one where the site's own containment is worth nothing to the job. Harrowbank hands a squad six ready-made pens — five switch bays and an oil bund, all cast concrete, all reading three escape rays bare — and this incident does not need one of them. What it needs is for the yard to be stripped while something walks it, and the only thing on the site that helps with that is a burning object placed as far from the transit case as a person can carry it. A squad that walks in with the draught's loadout has brought a beacon and stood behind it.

operations.name: Coldharbour cold storage, level 2
operations.distance: Forty minutes. The fifth time down that stair, and the first time the floor has hurt somebody who was standing still.
operations.mandate: Establish custody of whatever is in one of the four floor gullies on level 2 and transfer it to the stair head.
optional: No operative below two conditions at extraction
Lift a rime sample from an unoccupied gully
conditions: One attendant hospitalised with cold burns to both hands and no account of twenty minutes.
Both men who were on the floor are on site and both of them went back the following night on purpose.
Four gullies on the same run, all the same fitting, all with an old rime ring round them. The site does not know which one is meant.
operations._note: THE FIFTH OPERATION ON THIS FLOOR AND THE FIRST WITH A PRICE ON IT. Four operations' worth of correct knowledge about cold storage level 2 and none of it applies: the aisles do not matter, a camera does nothing at all, and the imager finds the thing in four seconds and then has no further job. What is left is a fee — eighteen unbroken seconds of something warm inside two metres — and the only thing on this floor that can pay it without a battery in it is a person. The optional line about conditions at extraction is not decoration; the minimum grade of this procedure has an injury in it by design.

_boardNote:
Nine operations, and every one of them is playable to custody — the board does not pad itself with contracts that do not exist. §18.1 does not allow the UI to lie about what is available, so a greyed-out entry would be a promise this build cannot keep. FOUR SITES CARRY NINE INCIDENTS: cold storage level 2 alone has five, the ninth floor of Ashlar has two, and Blackthorn Reserve and Harrowbank have one each. That is the whole of §15.2 in one column — the site is a variable and the incident is a variable, and they vary independently — and by the fifth trip down the same stair the point is no longer that the map is reused. It is that a squad arrives carrying four operations' worth of correct knowledge about that floor and has to work out which of it still applies. On the fifth, none of it does.

The column is deliberately not sorted by difficulty. Every entry is Field grade at clearance 1 and the order is the order they were authorised, because a board that ranked them would be answering the one question §18.4's planner exists to make the squad answer for itself.

containmentWing.framing: Entries record where it came from, what holding it costs, and what it has done since. They do not rank captures, do not count them as a score, and do not describe anything held here as a prize. An object in a cell is an ongoing operational commitment, not a result.
maintenanceNotes: Scheduled check. Cell log reviewed against the sensor bus; no discrepancy recorded.
Interior temperature drifted 0.4C over the interval. Within tolerance, logged, watched.
Monitor channel two reported a two-second dropout. Cause not established. Cell inspected and re-sealed.
Consumable draw above forecast for the interval. Requisition notified.

cells.label: Cell 1
cells.holding: Insulated, heated, sensor ports on the corridor bus. The only position rated for a thermal negative.

cells.label: Cell 2
cells.holding: General holding. Sealed door, one camera, no environmental control.

cells.label: Cell 3
cells.holding: Locker-scale. Objects and samples, not organisms. The extract fan has been on the list since March.

dossiers._designationNote: A provisional internal designation, not an SCP number. GDD §25.3 holds that a final designation is assigned only after the licensing record exists, and content/anomalies/graybox-draught.json carries `licensingRecordId: null`. Nothing in this build should print a number it has not earned the right to print.
dossiers.classFraming: A thermal negative that moves toward heat and cannot cross a sustained gradient above 40C. Not hostile in any sense the site can evidence; it is cold, and people are warm.
dossiers.holding: escort at 39C in a heated transit case, corridor cleared, two operatives
dossiers.operationalCost: Holding it costs a heated cell on continuous draw and a fortnightly gradient check. It has never tested the seal. It has never had to.

insights.text: Thermal is the only reliable observation channel. It records faithfully in that band and not at all in the visible one, so a camera that sees nothing is not evidence of absence.
insights.grants: A line on the operation card before the squad deploys.

insights.text: The gradient figure is 40C, sustained and continuous. A contour with a gap in it is not a fence, and the aisles on level 2 are 4.2m across.
insights.grants: The figure appears on the briefing instead of being inferred in the field.

insights.text: It goes to the warmest thing it can reach. A transit case held one degree under the threshold out-competes an operative; a tripod set down too near the case takes the case over the threshold and the lure stops working.
insights.grants: The archive files this as a procedure note rather than a hard-won field lesson.

dossiers.classFraming: Stationary under observation and fast without it. It reads at ambient in every band the site can instrument, so the only channel that records it is a person or a camera looking at it, and the record ends the moment the looking does.
dossiers.holding: two channels of continuous coverage on independent supplies, corridor cleared, three operatives
dossiers.operationalCost: Holding it costs two camera channels that must never both be down, and the cell's own draw is what its capability reaches for. The wing runs the corridor bus off the second supply for this reason and not for redundancy.

insights.text: It reads at ambient on thermal, in every state, at every distance. An imager pointed at it shows the aisle. The imager is not the wrong instrument for this floor; there is no right one.
insights.grants: The briefing stops listing the imager as a detection asset for this incident.

insights.text: Coverage is a resource the squad also needs for carrying, placing, powering and sealing. A camera holds it exactly as well as a person does and does not need to stand there, which is the whole procedure and the reason the cameras are the first thing its capability browns out.
insights.grants: A line on the operation card before the squad deploys.

insights.text: A moment of lost coverage does not release it. A second and a half does. The gap between those two figures is the entire margin a handover has, and it does not widen with practice.
insights.grants: The figure appears on the briefing instead of being learned at the cost of a contact.

dossiers.classFraming: A discrepancy rather than an object: five items in a set of eleven that are indistinguishable from the other six by eye, by weight and by every hand instrument the site issues. Nothing about it moves and nobody has been hurt by it.
dossiers.holding: the set held complete in one locker, count verified against the sheet at every check
dossiers.operationalCost: Holding it costs nothing but an accurate count, and that is the expensive part. A check that reports eleven without recounting is not a check, and the wing has been asked twice to explain why the interval is per-item.

insights.text: Each one is a four-degree sink. Three together read nearly eight degrees below ambient and are obvious from a doorway; one on its own reads under four and has to be stood over. The instrument the squad brought to fence a draught is the instrument that finds these, used the other way round.
insights.grants: A line on the operation card before the squad deploys.

insights.text: The case takes a mundane one silently and the count does not move. Nothing announces the mistake. Noticing that the number stayed still is the whole verification, and a squad that seals on a number it did not watch change has sealed on a guess.
insights.grants: The archive files this as a procedure note rather than a debrief finding.

insights.text: The total is on the stocktake sheet in the office and has never been on the HUD. Sealing on three of five is a legal, survivable, wrong answer that the operation does not report until the debrief.
insights.grants: The briefing names where the sheet is.

dossiers.classFraming: It moves toward sound and stops in silence. Heat does not stop it and walls do, which makes a building the only fence available and makes every powered object the site owns a lure.
dossiers.holding: escort with all carried equipment off, cell on the isolated corridor spur, two operatives
dossiers.operationalCost: Holding it costs the wing's extract fans on the north corridor, which have been switched to the manual schedule since the transfer. The consumable draw is trivial and the noise budget is not.

insights.text: A heater carries twenty-two metres, a floodlight ballast eleven, a power pack seven. On a cold-store floor those numbers are the fence and the bait. Here every one of them is a beacon, and a squad running the draught playbook has built a perfect lure around itself and switched it on.
insights.grants: A line on the operation card before the squad deploys.

insights.text: Two sources of comparable level at comparable range do not make a stronger lure. They make an unresolvable one, and it stops in the wrong place, which looks exactly like the rule failing and is the rule working.
insights.grants: The archive files this as a procedure note rather than a field lesson paid for with a contact.

insights.text: At two metres: 29.6 dB standing still, 35.1 crouch-walking, 48.0 walking, against a 46 dB threshold. Crouch stops being a way to be shorter and becomes the approach.
insights.grants: The figures appear on the briefing instead of being found by walking at it once.

dossiers.classFraming: It does not move and it does not choose. Anything warm that comes within a metre and a half of it is taken, and it will not be observed while it is holding something. The site records one fatality and one serious burn, neither of them the result of being approached deliberately.
dossiers.holding: sealed transit case on continuous supply, no camera on the cell interior, two operatives
dossiers.operationalCost: Holding it costs a case that is never allowed to go flat and a cell whose interior channel stays off. The monitor bus records the door and the corridor and nothing else, which is a documented exception and not an outage.

insights.text: It reads at ambient on every instrument in the manifest, in every state, from every distance. What the imager is for on this floor is the wake it leaves: a band of thawed and refrozen floor, and boot prints in it that are not the squad's.
insights.grants: A line on the operation card before the squad deploys.

insights.text: A camera left pointing near the case does not stall the operation, it makes it stutter: take, let go, take, on a three-and-a-half second cycle, with the drain running through half of it. The seal is genuinely available in the other half. The case's twelve minutes come out at about five.
insights.grants: The archive files this as a procedure note rather than a debrief arithmetic problem.

insights.text: Three operations' worth of correct knowledge about this floor is aimed at the wrong thing. The only habit that survives is the one nobody thinks of as a habit: get the case out of cargo and get it powered before anything else happens.
insights.grants: The briefing carries the sequence rather than the squad reconstructing it.

dossiers.classFraming: Attention sets it rigid and inattention slackens it. Being watched is not a restraint here, it is the condition under which nothing can be done: the opposite of SW-11, on the same quantity, and the wing has asked twice that the two not be filed together.
dossiers.holding: sealed case, cell interior channel off, door channel only, two operatives
dossiers.operationalCost: Holding it costs the same interior channel CH-02 costs, for the opposite reason: a camera on this one holds it rigid indefinitely and there is then no way to open the cell. The extract fan is on the list.

insights.text: Setting is instantaneous and from any state. Slackening takes five continuous seconds of nobody and no camera holding it in view. An operative who glances round to check where the case is has spent five seconds they have to buy again.
insights.grants: A line on the operation card before the squad deploys.

insights.text: A sightline is stopped by eleven millimetres of plasterboard exactly as completely as by a concrete crosswall. On the ninth floor of Ashlar that means a wall which stops nothing at all can hide you from this, and hiding is the entire containment.
insights.grants: The archive files the standing position rather than the squad finding it by being seen.

insights.text: The five-second figure sits inside the seven-second contact cooldown, so an operative who takes station correctly eats exactly one contact and not two. A squad that does not know the figure is five will turn back round at three and buy nothing.
insights.grants: Both figures appear on the briefing.

dossiers.classFraming: A thermal negative with weight in it that holds a set of ordinary objects and cannot be lifted while it holds any of them. It moves toward the hottest thing it can find, sits on that thing for about half a minute, and then chooses again. Concrete stops it and a heat gradient does not, which is the reverse of GB-04 on both counts and the wing has asked that the two not be filed together.
dossiers.holding: sealed case with its own ballast inside it, locker-scale, contents not to be separated from it under any circumstances
dossiers.operationalCost: Cheap to hold and expensive to handle. It draws no environmental control at all — nothing in the file is about temperature once the lid is over — but the case cannot be opened and cannot be inventoried, because taking one stone out of it is the same act as releasing it. Cell 3 therefore holds a sealed container the wing is not permitted to look inside, which the standing orders had no wording for and now do.

insights.text: It will not go in a box while it owns anything. Every piece of it that is loose has to be in the case and nothing else may be, because a case with the wrong thing in it counts as full of nothing.
insights.grants: A line on the operation card before the squad deploys.

insights.text: It goes to the hottest object on the site and not to the nearest person, and the transit case at 39C is an object. Whatever is left burning is where it will be, and it is only dangerous on the way there.
insights.grants: The archive files the decoy as procedure rather than the squad discovering it by being walked at.

insights.text: Turning the case out is the only way to clear a wrong object from it, and it is also what puts every part of it back on the ground. Two recovery crews have now written down the same afternoon: the skip went, and the shift after that was the worst one they had.
insights.grants: The briefing carries the warning instead of the debrief carrying the explanation.

dossiers.classFraming: A thermal negative that does not move, does not respond to being watched and does not respond to sound. What it responds to is warmth staying inside two metres of it without a break, and after enough of that it stops and will go in a box. It is the only entry in this file whose containment has a price rather than a procedure.
dossiers.holding: sealed case, heater cycling, cell interior channel on, one operative
dossiers.operationalCost: It wants Cell 1, and Cell 1 is where GB-04 is. That is a scheduling problem rather than a technical one and it is written here because it is going to be somebody's afternoon: the wing has one position rated for a thermal negative and two things that read as one. Holding cost otherwise is low — a sealed case draws nothing from it, because it only takes while something warm is inside the reach and the reach is inside the case.

insights.text: Something warm has to stay inside two metres of it, unbroken, for eighteen seconds. It does not care what the warm thing is and it does not care who is watching.
insights.grants: A line on the operation card before the squad deploys.

insights.text: Three seconds after it stops, anything warm still standing in its reach starts the whole fee again from nothing. There is no partial credit and no warning beyond the rime edge starting to move.
insights.grants: The archive files the last move rather than the squad losing a fee to it.

insights.text: Anything with a cell in it inside those two metres empties about twelve times faster than rated, so a portable heater will pay the fee once and will not pay it twice. The only payer with nothing to drain is a person, and two of the three site staff who have worked this out did it by accident.
insights.grants: The briefing carries the trade instead of a squad spending a case's cells finding it.

_insightNote: Insights grant CONTEXT ONLY — a line the briefing did not previously carry. None of them changes a number the anomaly obeys, because GDD §12.1 says progression must not turn horror into immunity. A squad that has read all three still has to build the fence.
